types.oie_definition: A specific day, month, or year in the calendar.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, or year in the calendar. Also called calendar date, specific day, point in time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation. Also called nation, state, realm.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater

Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Continent

candidates.label: Person

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.oie_definition: Content (audio, video, images, text) that is created, stored, and distributed in digital formats.
types.embedding_query_text: Digital Media: Content (audio, video, images, text) that is created, stored, and distributed in digital formats. Also called electronic media, online content.

chosen_type.label: MediaObject
chosen_type.justification: MediaObject explicitly covers digital media like 'image' and 'video', which aligns with the mentions.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: TextObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a text file, which can contain unformatted text or markup like HTML. Also called text file object, digital text file, document media. Examples: a plain text file (.txt), an HTML file, a Markdown document. Distinct from TextDigitalDocument, which is a structured digital document primarily composed of text.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

types.oie_definition: An online service or site that facilitates interaction and content sharing among users.
types.embedding_query_text: Social Media Platform: An online service or site that facilitates interaction and content sharing among users. Also called social network, online community.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service or site that facilitates interaction and content sharing among users.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate represents the platform itself; Service is a suitable parent for an online service.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

types.oie_definition: An observable event or occurrence in the Earth's atmosphere.
types.embedding_query_text: Atmospheric Phenomenon: An observable event or occurrence in the Earth's atmosphere. Also called weather phenomenon, atmospheric event.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: A 'smoke plume' is an observable occurrence, fitting the general Event type.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative count of occurrences.
types.embedding_query_text: Number of Events: A quantitative count of occurrences. Also called event count, incident tally.

chosen_type.label: CountOfEvents
chosen_type.definition: A quantitative count of occurrences.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type refers to a count of events, not the event itself; Quantity is a suitable parent for a count.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

types.oie_definition: A particular place or position.
types.embedding_query_text: Location: A particular place or position. Also called place, site, spot.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Place type directly matches the definition and explicitly includes 'site' in its aliases.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.oie_definition: A densely populated area, typically smaller than a city but larger than a village.
types.embedding_query_text: Town: A densely populated area, typically smaller than a city but larger than a village. Also called settlement, community, municipality.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org City type's definition explicitly includes 'town', making it a good fit.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CampingPitch
candidates.comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

types.oie_definition: A structure used as a home or dwelling.
types.embedding_query_text: Residential Building: A structure used as a home or dwelling. Also called house, dwelling, residence.

chosen_type.label: House
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org House type directly matches the definition and mention of a building used for habitation.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.

candidates.label: Apartment
candidates.comment: An Apartment is a self-contained housing unit, a type of residential real estate that occupies only part of a building. Also called flat, condo, dwelling unit, residential unit. Examples: a studio apartment, a two-bedroom flat, a penthouse suite, a loft. Distinct from ApartmentComplex, which is a building containing multiple apartments.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative count of structures.
types.embedding_query_text: Number of Buildings: A quantitative count of structures. Also called building count, structure tally.

chosen_type.label: CountOfBuildings
chosen_type.definition: A quantitative count of structures.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type refers to a count of buildings, not a type of building; Quantity is a suitable parent for a count.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

types.oie_definition: A place where trains stop for passengers to get on or off, or for goods to be loaded or unloaded.
types.embedding_query_text: Train Station: A place where trains stop for passengers to get on or off, or for goods to be loaded or unloaded. Also called railway station, depot.

chosen_type.label: TrainStation
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org TrainStation type directly matches the definition and mention of a train station.

candidates.label: TrainStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

candidates.label: TrainTrip
candidates.comment: A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip. Examples: a cross-country train journey, a daily commute by train, a scenic train ride through the mountains.

candidates.label: BusStation
candidates.comment: A BusStation is a CivicStructure serving as a central terminal where buses depart, arrive, and transfer passengers. Also called bus terminal, coach station, bus depot. Examples: Port Authority Bus Terminal, Victoria Coach Station, a local intercity bus station. Distinct from BusStop, which is a smaller, temporary stopping point.

candidates.label: TrainReservation
candidates.comment: A reservation specifically for travel on a commercial train line. Also called train booking, rail reservation, seat booking. Examples: a reservation for a high-speed train, a sleeper car booking, a ticket for a scenic rail journey.

types.oie_definition: A collection of individuals.
types.embedding_query_text: Group of People: A collection of individuals. Also called crowd, assembly, collective.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: A group of 'local officials' is a group of people with a particular purpose, fitting the definition of Organization.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

types.oie_definition: One of the four main points of a compass: north, south, east, or west.
types.embedding_query_text: Cardinal Direction: One of the four main points of a compass: north, south, east, or west. Also called compass point, direction.

chosen_type.label: CardinalDirection
chosen_type.definition: One of the four main points of a compass: north, south, east, or west.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate represents a 'Cardinal Direction'; QualitativeValue is a suitable parent for a descriptive value.

candidates.label: SteeringPositionValue
candidates.comment: A value indicating the steering position of a vehicle. Also called steering side, driver's side, vehicle control position. Examples: 'LeftHandDriving', 'RightHandDriving'.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

types.oie_definition: A public service such as electricity, water, or internet.
types.embedding_query_text: Utility Service: A public service such as electricity, water, or internet. Also called public utility, essential service.

chosen_type.label: Service
chosen_type.justification: Electricity is an intangible offering provided to the public, fitting the general Service type.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: EmergencyService
candidates.comment: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.

types.oie_definition: An entity dedicated to conducting systematic investigation to establish facts or principles.
types.embedding_query_text: Research Organization: An entity dedicated to conducting systematic investigation to establish facts or principles. Also called research institute, think tank.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org ResearchOrganization type directly matches the definition and mention of an entity dedicated to research.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

types.oie_definition: An interruption or breakdown in the provision of a service.
types.embedding_query_text: Service Disruption: An interruption or breakdown in the provision of a service. Also called outage, interruption, breakdown.

chosen_type.label: ServiceDisruption
chosen_type.definition: An interruption or breakdown in the provision of a service.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate specifically represents a 'Service Disruption'; Error (an InstantaneousEvent) is a suitable parent for a breakdown or failure.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

candidates.label: BroadcastService
candidates.comment: A BroadcastService is a Service that delivers content via broadcast, either over the air or online. Also called broadcasting service, media transmission service, content delivery service. Examples: a national television network, a satellite radio provider, an internet radio service.

candidates.label: RadioBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A RadioBroadcastService is a BroadcastService delivering radio content via broadcast over the air or online. Also called radio service, broadcast radio. Examples: BBC Radio 4, NPR, a local FM radio station, an internet radio stream.

types.oie_definition: An act of helping or doing work for someone, or a system supplying a public need.
types.embedding_query_text: Service: An act of helping or doing work for someone, or a system supplying a public need. Also called provision, utility, amenity.

chosen_type.label: Service
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Service type directly matches the definition and mentions of offerings like 'connectivity'.

candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. types.oie_definition: A classification of data which tells the interpreter how the programmer intends to use the data.
types.embedding_query_text: Data Type: A classification of data which tells the interpreter how the programmer intends to use the data. Also called information category, data format.

chosen_type.label: DataKind
chosen_type.definition: A classification or category of data.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type refers to a kind of data ('telemetry data'), not a Schema.org DataType (like Integer or String).

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: XPathType
candidates.comment: A data type representing an XPath expression, used for navigating XML or HTML documents. Also called XPath expression, XML Path Language, query path. Examples: "/bookstore/book[price>35]", "//title", "id('myElement')".

types.oie_definition: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred.
types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called proportion, fraction, ratio.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: A percentage is a numerical value, which is best represented by the Schema.org Number data type.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

types.oie_definition: The state of something with regard to its appearance, quality, or working order.
types.embedding_query_text: Condition: The state of something with regard to its appearance, quality, or working order. Also called state, status, situation.

chosen_type.label: Condition
chosen_type.definition: The state of something with regard to its appearance, quality, or working order.
chosen_type.justification: StatusEnumeration is for types of status, not the condition itself; Thing is the most general suitable parent for an abstract state.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: OfferItemCondition
candidates.comment: OfferItemCondition is an enumeration listing possible conditions for an item being offered. Also called item state, product condition, quality status. Examples: NewCondition, UsedCondition, RefurbishedCondition, DamagedCondition. Distinct from OfferShippingDetails, which describes shipping logistics.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

types.oie_definition: A specific point or period in the day, often expressed with hours and minutes.
types.embedding_query_text: Time: A specific point or period in the day, often expressed with hours and minutes. Also called moment, hour, clock time.

chosen_type.label: Time
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Time type directly matches the definition and mention of a specific point in time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.oie_definition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
types.embedding_query_text: Power Generator: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. Also called electric generator, dynamo.

chosen_type.label: PowerGenerator
chosen_type.definition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate specifically represents a 'Power Generator'; Product is a suitable parent for a manufactured machine.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: MotorizedBicycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense). Examples: a pedal-assist electric bicycle, a bicycle with a small gas engine kit. Distinct from Motorcycle, which is designed from the ground up as a motor vehicle.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

types.oie_definition: Resources kept ready for use in an emergency.
types.embedding_query_text: Emergency Supply: Resources kept ready for use in an emergency. Also called emergency provisions, backup resources.

chosen_type.label: EmergencySupply
chosen_type.definition: Resources kept ready for use in an emergency.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate specifically represents 'Emergency Supply'; Product is a suitable parent for resources or goods.

candidates.label: EmergencyService
candidates.comment: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: ItemAvailability
candidates.comment: ItemAvailability is an enumeration of possible product availability options. Also called product status, stock status, inventory condition. Examples: 'InStock', 'OutOfStock', 'PreOrder', 'InStoreOnly'.

candidates.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
candidates.comment: An OfficeEquipmentStore is a local business that sells supplies and equipment for offices. Also called office supply store, stationery shop, business equipment retailer. Examples: Staples, Office Depot, a local stationery shop. Distinct from ComputerStore, which specializes in computers.

candidates.label: ConvenienceStore
candidates.comment: A local business retail store offering a limited range of everyday items, often with extended hours. Also called corner store, mini-mart, quick shop. Examples: 7-Eleven, Circle K, a local neighborhood market, a gas station store. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1. Also called calendar year, annum.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: A 'year' is a period of time, which aligns with the definition of Duration.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.oie_definition: A piece of data relating to the structure of populations.
types.embedding_query_text: Demographic Statistic: A piece of data relating to the structure of populations. Also called population data, demographic figure.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: A 'pre-war population' is a set of instances (people) defined by a specific constraint, fitting StatisticalPopulation.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

types.oie_definition: A city or town with a harbor where ships load and unload.
types.embedding_query_text: Port City: A city or town with a harbor where ships load and unload. Also called seaport, harbor city.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: A 'Port City' is primarily a city, and the Schema.org City type is the most appropriate general classification.

mentions: Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: TrainStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

types.oie_definition: A structured body of armed forces.
types.embedding_query_text: Military Organization: A structured body of armed forces. Also called armed forces, military unit, defense force.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: A 'military' or 'forces' are organizations that are part of a governmental body, fitting GovernmentOrganization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.oie_definition: An official document or statement providing information about military operations or status.
types.embedding_query_text: Military Report: An official document or statement providing information about military operations or status. Also called military brief, operational update.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: An 'operational update' is a type of official document providing information, fitting the Report type.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

types.oie_definition: A specific part or section of a military installation.
types.embedding_query_text: Military Facility Component: A specific part or section of a military installation. Also called military site element, defense infrastructure part.

chosen_type.label: MilitaryFacilityComponent
chosen_type.definition: A specific part or section of a military installation.
chosen_type.justification: DefenceEstablishment is the facility itself, not a component; Place is a suitable general parent for a site or section.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Airport
candidates.comment: An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Examples: London Heathrow Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport. Distinct from Airline, which is the company operating flights.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: WebPageElement
candidates.comment: A distinct part or component within a web page. Also called page component, web element, UI element. Examples: a navigation menu, an image, a form, a table.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.
